title: 3rd Truth Ease Amid Speed And Multiplicity And The Gradelessness Of Power

questions.question: What kinds of living things are especially mentioned in this passage?
questions.answer: Plants and animals are especially mentioned.

questions.question: How are these living things said to be made in regard to speed and order?
questions.answer: They are made very quickly and in a very orderly way.

questions.question: What other qualities are joined with that speed?
questions.answer: Great skill, ease, care, and beauty are joined with it.

questions.question: Even though there are very many living things mixed together, what problem does the passage say does not happen?
questions.answer: There is no mix-up, no disorder, and no lack in their creation.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can do this kind of creating?
questions.answer: Only the One unique Creator can do it.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about that power?
questions.answer: It teaches that nothing is hard for that power.

questions.question: What comparison is made between stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Creating stars is just as easy as creating atoms.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the biggest things and the smallest things?
questions.answer: The biggest and the smallest are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: How does the passage compare making a whole kind of creature with making one member of it?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about bringing the earth back to life and bringing a tree to life?
questions.answer: Reviving the whole earth is as easy as reviving one tree.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a huge tree and a tiny seed?
questions.answer: Making a mountain-like tree is as easy as making a very small seed.

questions.question: What main lesson about Allah’s power should a student learn from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfect and unlimited, so creating many, great, or tiny things is all easy for Him.

questions.question: What is the main topic of this part of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about how Allah creates living things with perfect power, speed, and order.

questions.question: Which two groups of living things are used as special examples?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: Does the passage describe creation as slow and messy or fast and well-arranged?
questions.answer: It describes creation as fast and well-arranged.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this work cannot belong to an ordinary being?
questions.answer: Because such work needs a power for which nothing is difficult.

questions.question: What does “nothing appears difficult” teach about the Creator?
questions.answer: It teaches that His power has no weakness or limit.

questions.question: How does the passage help us compare one tiny thing with one huge thing?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: What example shows that a whole group and one single member are alike for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: A whole species and one individual of that species are alike in ease.

questions.question: What example shows life being given on two different levels?
questions.answer: The whole earth being brought to life and one tree being brought to life.

questions.question: What example shows that size does not matter to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: A towering tree and a seed smaller than a fingernail are both easy for Him to make.

questions.question: If a student sees many kinds of plants growing in an organized way, what idea from this passage does that support?
questions.answer: It supports that Allah creates with perfect order, ease, and power.

questions.question: In this passage, what is special about the way plants and animals are created?
questions.answer: They are created quickly, neatly, skillfully, and with great value.

questions.question: What does the passage say about ease and skill working together?
questions.answer: It says creation happens easily but still with amazing skill and care.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from this perfect creation?
questions.answer: It concludes that only one unique Creator with unlimited power can do it.

questions.question: What does the comparison of stars and atoms teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that huge things and tiny things are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the comparison of a species and one member teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that making many is no harder than making one for Allah.

questions.question: What does reviving the whole earth compared with reviving a tree show?
questions.answer: It shows that giving life on a great scale or a small scale is equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Why is the example of a big tree and a tiny seed helpful for understanding the message?
questions.answer: It helps us see that size does not limit Allah’s power.

questions.question: What belief about Allah is strengthened by these examples?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah is all-powerful.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly about human effort or Divine power?
questions.answer: It is mainly about Divine power.

questions.question: Write the main idea of the whole passage in one short sentence.
questions.answer: Allah creates all living things with perfect power, and nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with complete swiftness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the neatness of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with complete order.

questions.question: Besides being fast and orderly, how else are living things made?
questions.answer: They are made with skill, care, ability, and beauty.

questions.question: Why is it amazing that living things are made in abundance?
questions.answer: Because even with so many of them, each one is still made properly.

questions.question: What word best describes the being who can create without any difficulty?
questions.answer: Unique.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying that nothing is difficult for that power?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s power is unlimited and never strained.

questions.question: How are stars and atoms used in the passage?
questions.answer: They are used to show that very large and very small things are the same for Allah’s power.

questions.question: How are a universal thing and a small particular thing compared?
questions.answer: They are said to be equally easy to create.

questions.question: What does the passage say about making the earth alive again, compared to making a tree alive?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to notice by saying these deeds happen before our eyes?
questions.answer: It wants us to notice the clear signs of Allah in the world we see.

questions.question: What is the “Third Truth” mainly trying to prove?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove the greatness and ease of Allah’s power in creation.

questions.question: Which created things are named first in the explanation?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how they are created in large numbers?
questions.answer: They are created in large numbers without losing order or beauty.

questions.question: How does the passage connect abundance with value?
questions.answer: It says things can be very many and still be precious and special.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that there is no confusion among many created beings?
questions.answer: We can understand that their Creator has perfect control.

questions.question: Why can only one unique Creator do this, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because only such a Creator has power for which nothing is hard.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing stars with atoms?
questions.answer: The point is that size makes no difference to Allah.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing a species with one member?
questions.answer: The point is that number makes no difference to Allah.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing the whole earth with one tree?
questions.answer: The point is that a vast work and a small work are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing a huge tree with a tiny seed?
questions.answer: The point is that Allah creates both with the same ease.

questions.question: What is one strong conclusion a student should make after reading this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone has the perfect power to create everything, great or small.

questions.question: What kinds of qualities in creation does this passage ask us to think about?
questions.answer: It asks us to think about speed, order, skill, ease, abundance, and value.

questions.question: Why is it important that ease is mentioned with great skill?
questions.answer: Because it shows perfect power can do amazing work without difficulty.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention abundance and intermingling?
questions.answer: To show that even when many things are together, each one is still made correctly.

questions.question: What result shows that this creation is perfect?
questions.answer: There is no confusion and no deficiency.

questions.question: What kind of being is described as able to create in this way?
questions.answer: A single unique Being with unlimited power.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating stars and atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating the greatest thing and the smallest thing?
questions.answer: It says there is no difference in difficulty for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating all members of a kind with creating one member?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage compare reviving the earth and reviving a tree?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy acts of giving life.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the example of a very tiny seed and a very large tree?
questions.answer: The lesson is that Allah’s power is not limited by size.

questions.question: If someone says a huge creation must be hard while a tiny one must be easy, how would this passage answer?
questions.answer: It would answer that both are equally easy for Allah’s power.
